name: React Native
summary: A cross-platform UI framework that transforms JavaScript React element trees through a C++ shadow tree and layout pipeline into native host views on platform UI threads.

features.name: Element-to-shadow-tree rendering
features.description: React Native reduces JavaScript React elements to host components and creates corresponding C++ shadow nodes. Parent-child relationships in the element tree are represented in the React Shadow Tree, while composite JavaScript components do not become native views themselves.
benefits: Separates declarative JavaScript composition from platform view creation
Provides a common intermediate representation for multiple host platforms
Allows immutable shadow-tree updates and cloning for concurrent renderer work
costs: The intermediate representation adds memory and transformation work
Component behavior must respect the distinction between composite and host components
Platform-specific measurements remain visible at the host boundary

features.name: Render, commit, and mount pipeline
features.description: The renderer separates rendering the element and shadow trees, committing layout and promoting the next tree, and mounting a diff as native host-view mutations. Yoga participates in layout calculation and the mounting layer turns the resulting tree into platform view operations.
benefits: Makes layout and native mutation stages explicit
Allows tree diffing to minimize host-view mutations
Supports asynchronous work between JavaScript, background, and UI execution contexts
costs: State can exist at several pipeline stages before pixels are visible
Scheduling and interruption behavior complicate debugging and latency reasoning
Layout and mount correctness depend on platform host-view constraints

features.name: Thread-safe platform renderer boundary
features.description: React Native distributes renderer work across JavaScript and UI threads while restricting host-view manipulation to the UI thread. Immutable C++ data structures and JSI-backed references provide the thread-safe boundary between JavaScript logic and native rendering internals.
benefits: Keeps platform view mutation on the thread required by native UI toolkits
Permits render work and state preparation to be scheduled separately from mounting
Provides a shared integration model for Android and iOS host views
costs: Cross-thread scheduling and synchronization affect responsiveness
Native modules and views must obey platform thread rules
The abstraction does not remove differences between platform view capabilities

mathematical_views.question: How does a JavaScript React element tree become a laid-out and mounted native host-view tree?
assumptions: Element, shadow, and host-view trees are distinct representations
Render, commit, and mount are modeled as ordered stages with possible asynchronous execution
The view abstracts React scheduling details and native drawing implementation

mathematical_views.question: Which renderer transitions may occur on JavaScript, background, and UI threads while preserving host-view safety?
assumptions: Only the UI thread mutates platform host views
Immutable shadow-tree snapshots can be shared across renderer stages
The model treats interruption and priority as transition scheduling constraints, not guarantees of frame timing

benefits: A portable declarative representation can feed multiple native platforms
costs: Intermediate trees and cloning add representation and lifecycle overhead

benefits: Explicit stages enable layout calculation and native mutation diffing
costs: Pipeline staging introduces latency and more states to observe

benefits: Native UI thread rules are isolated behind a common renderer contract
costs: Thread scheduling and platform-specific host behavior remain integration costs
